title: The wager
subtopic: S7 — The bet, the route and the bank
learning_goal: Know the bet, the shape of the route and what became of the bank; feel the click of a plan.

narration.script: A card table at the Reform, an afternoon in October 1872. A newspaper says eighty days is now possible. One of the players says it lies. Eight legs, and the days land as they go. They add up to eighty. Twenty thousand pounds — half his fortune. Back in this room on the twenty-first of December, a quarter to nine. Eighty days. Nineteen hundred and twenty hours. A hundred and fifteen thousand two hundred minutes. Fogg's bank lasted two hundred and thirty-three years — until one trader lost eight hundred and twenty-seven million pounds and killed it in 1995. Verne gives him one line worth keeping: the unforeseen does not exist. And the turn, in Verne's words: the train leaves for Dover at a quarter before nine.
